candidate.answerReason: A linear pair has opposite noncommon rays, so its angles sum to 180° and are supplementary. Supplementary angles need not form a linear pair.

methods.label: Use the definition of a linear pair
methods.explanation: Angles in a linear pair have a common side, and their other sides are opposite rays, so their measures add up to \(180^\circ\) and they are supplementary. However, two supplementary angles do not necessarily have a common side and do not necessarily form a linear pair.
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 7 definitions of rays, linear pairs and supplementary angles.
